source.title: Beyond Scaling Laws: Understanding Transformer Performance with Associative Memory
source.authors: Xue-Yan Niu; Bo Bai; Lei Deng; Wei Han

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Figure contents are not available as numerical data in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports validation-loss behavior over training time in its own Transformer experiments, bearing on epoch-wise double descent, but does not reproduce the original double-descent sweeps.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly says test losses began to ascend after repeated training, and reports validation-loss minima over training runs. This bears on the time-course version, though the full fall-rise-fall shape is not reported. The Table 3 MSE values are used to select D* and are not recorded as outcome rows. The reported model-size/data-size ratios are recorded as findings not covered by a claim version; they do not measure whether more data raises test error.
record.test_reason: A theory paper modelling Transformers as associative memory. It cites Belkin and Nakkiran only as background. Its OpenELM runs report a validation-loss minimum followed by a rise, which is ordinary overfitting; no second descent is sought or reported. It runs no sweep of model size, epochs or samples aimed at a double-descent peak, so its results do not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors model Transformer layers as associative memories using a distance-based layer-wise energy and a majorization-minimization global energy. They derive that cross-entropy loss is bounded below (about 1) and that the optimal balance for well-separated patterns is N = O(D²). They call their experiments preliminary and note that early and delayed stopping can both hurt performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops an associative-memory and energy-function framework and trains or analyzes Transformers; it does not reproduce the original double-descent sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported validation-loss minima and ascent are tied to training time and dataset/model configurations; numerical curve comparisons by condition are not stated in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: For three OpenELM sizes, the selected D* gives N/D*² of 8.71, 8.79 and 8.38 (×10^-10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For well-separated memorized data, the optimal model size scales roughly as N = O(D²).

fits_no_version.finding: With repeated training on reduced data, validation loss reaches a minimum (about step 6000 for Model 1) and then rises, while training loss plateaus.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Repeated training of small Transformers on limited data shows a classical overfitting minimum in validation loss.

record.problems: The authors call the numerical experiments preliminary and computationally constrained. The temporal loss curves are presented graphically without numerical values in the text, and the paper does not report a full fall-rise-fall validation-loss trajectory.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix F.2 training losses around 1 do not measure test error over training time. Appendix F.3 Table 3 MSE entries are used to select D* and are therefore omitted. The GPT-2 nearest-neighbor distances concern pattern radius, not the claim versions.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep at fixed data reporting test error around the interpolation threshold.
No training-time curve examined for a second descent; only a validation minimum and subsequent rise are mentioned.
Data size varies only to select D*; no test of more data raising test error.
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.
No label-noise, multiple-descent or regularization tests.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V2 link and its limits_scope label are removed. A validation-loss rise after a minimum is standard overfitting and says nothing for or against a second descent, which the study never looks for. The paper's references to double descent (Belkin, Nakkiran, d'Ascoli) and to inverted-U scaling (Murty) are citations only.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep at fixed training data reports test error falling, peaking near interpolation, and falling again.
The study reports validation-loss minima and subsequent ascent, but does not report a complete fall-rise-fall curve or test it over epochs specifically.
The study varies data size to identify selected model/data combinations, but does not report that increasing sample size raises test error near an interpolation threshold.
No cross-model-class test of a general double-descent curve is reported.
The study proposes a model-size/data-size relationship, not a single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across axes.
No test of noise-driven peaks, multiple descent, or optimally tuned regularization removing a peak is reported.
The study does not compare double descent with a curve using an effective parameter count.

rows.baseline: Minimum validation loss; numerical value not stated
rows.value: The authors state that test losses had begun to ascend after repeated training.
rows.note: The paper does not describe the full temporal curve as fall-rise-fall or provide numerical curve values in the text.
rows.check: The row records a loss ascent after the validation minimum, i.e. a single U-shaped overfitting curve. V2 needs a fall-rise-fall trajectory; the paper neither trains far enough to show nor looks for a second fall. The row therefore cannot show V2's effect and should not be linked to V2.
